title: Atomic graph patterns + token mapping for Console metric surfaces
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Create an atomic set of graph and metric card patterns plus a clear mapping from visual tokens (spacing, color, typography, elevation) to component implementations used across Redwood Console dashboards, rollout banners, and cost-insights views.

Scope: inventory existing graph types (time series, bar, stacked area, sparkline), metric cards, rollout banners, and the cost breakdown UI. Define tokens needed for consistent rendering at multiple densities (compact, default, expanded). Produce Figma library components, a token mapping table for engineers, and a short accessibility checklist for each pattern.
acceptance_criteria: Figma library with 1x (default) and compact variants for: time-series chart, small sparkline, metric card, rollout banner, cost-insight line item.
Token mapping doc (CSS / tokens.json) that lists token name, purpose, recommended values, and component consumers.
Two prototype pages in Figma showing dashboards: (a) KPI dashboard with mixed charts and cards, (b) Rollout status page with banner + card stack, demonstrating tokens applied.
Accessibility notes added for color contrast, keyboard focus, and tooltip / aria labeling for charts.
Engineering sign-off (ENG-3456) that patterns can be implemented without additional runtime props beyond token mapping.
Design consistency review completed and comments resolved.
A short migration plan for replacing at least one old dashboard component in production (cost-insights) with the new tokens in the next release.
Documentation page stub in Confluence with token table and usage guidelines.

decision_log: 2026-02-10 - Decision: Use semantic token prefixes 'md-' (medium), 'sp-' (spacing), 'c-' (color) for clearer mapping to runtime config.
2026-02-18 - Decision: Create two density modes (default, compact) controlled by an outer container token rather than per-component props.
2026-02-25 - Decision: Standardize chart axis label font to UI/label-12 and use c-text-strong for axis to meet contrast.
2026-03-03 - Decision: Rollout banner will use elevation token e-2 and constrained max-height to avoid jumpiness across rollouts.
notes: Primary aim is to reduce UI variance across metric surfaces and provide a single source of truth for engineers. Keep the initial token set intentionally small and extensible; focus on high-impact tokens first (color, spacing, type, elevation).
migration_plan: Phase 1: Replace static metric card CSS in cost-insights with token-driven classes (ENG-3456)
Phase 2: Swap sparkline instance to new component in a canary route; monitor console cost and render latency
Phase 3: Full rollout behind feature flag with rollback plan and observability hooks
